Science comes only from sources whose terms allow use in an AI product (checked on 4 October 2026, the additions on 6 October 2026; see SOURCES.md): U.S. government science agencies (public domain, including NIST and the National Library of Medicine), ESO and NOIRLab press-release texts (CC BY 4.0), IAU press releases (CC BY 4.0, from the IAU archive hosted on eso.org), UC Berkeley Understanding Evolution (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), open university courses and textbooks (Open Yale Courses, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0; LibreTexts, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per page) and Our World in Data (CC BY 4.0). Wikipedia was replaced by these on 6 October 2026. Excluded: NASA, Hubble and Webb sites (their guidelines restrict AI use), OpenStax (no ingestion into AI products without written permission), the A.D.A.M. encyclopedia inside MedlinePlus (/ency/, AI use prohibited), ESA, CK-12 and the National Academies (all rights reserved). Saudi scholarly sources (binbaz.org.sa, binothaimeen.net; alifta.gov.sa for referrals) are used for explanation and creed with attribution; verse meanings still come only from the approved tafsir sources.
